source_text: Community interpretations parallel khafd with male circumcision (khatna), viewing both as complementary rites of passage performed around age seven that instill self-control and sectarian loyalty, thereby sustaining high adherence rates—evidenced by 56% of surveyed Bohra women attributing the practice to doctrinal requirements—which bolsters intra-community cohesion and obedience to the Dai's interpretive authority. [44]
